So you and Nenad Deronjic were in Konjevic Polje at the same time for two or three days and you didn't see each other, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I can confirm that during the three or four days that I spent in Konjevic Polje was not at the check-point where I was working [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: KW558 expressly recalled four persons walking towards the house and these four persons were you, Dusko Neskovic, Hasan Salihovic, and Resid Sinanovic. So his recollection is wrong, in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: This Neskovic person, who is that? I don't know him. I don't know him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Well, in KW558 testimony, you and Neskovic were together and were bringing these two prisoners to the house.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: No. I can confirm that it was I who took Sinanovic to that building. I did alone. There was no one else with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I have one thing to clarify. Could we ask the witness to excuse himself for a moment? Yes, our usher will escort you to outside the courtroom for a moment. Could the Chamber move into private session, briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, just while we are waiting for the witness, on a scheduling issue since this is the only witness we have for today I would suggest that we move forward as much as possible to complete his testimony without taking our lunch break if we are able to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long do you think you need?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I think I've been given 45 minutes but I will try, I'm not sure how many minutes I've already used but I will try to make it in a shorter time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: One of the judicial members have a meeting at 12.30, unless the whole proceedings could be concluded by 12.30, we need to go on, as originally planned.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Peric. Yes, we will continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So I understand that your testimony at paragraph 20, that I was about to talk about, you said that when you entered the room, "I saw that there were some other Muslims inside." So is it correct that apart from Resid that you were bringing, you saw other Muslims inside the room, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Yes, there were two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has heard the testimony of one of these Muslim who was detained in that house, and he saw you in the house. There is a problem with the --

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: The volume is too low. Now it's all right. It's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I was saying the Chamber heard the testimony of one of these detainees. He testified that he saw you in the house, that you went to the room later on, you took four detainees, you walked them to the warehouse at the intersection, and that you were present at the warehouse when the prisoners were forced to undress and while they were beaten up. I see that in your statement you reject most of these allegation, but I'm asking you again, did you go to the house, pick four of these detainees, brought them to the warehouse and left them there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: All right. So let's go to see what you said about KDZ065's testimony in your statement. At paragraph 31 you said: "Witness KDZ065 testified" -- sorry, I need to find the -- yeah, "testified that after being beaten the prisoners were told to put on their clothes, they were then led into a bus driven by a blond female driver. That part isn't true. I was working at the check-point in Konjevic Polje. And was looking at all the drivers of the buses as they were passing by. I never saw or heard of any woman bus driver working at that time. That would have been very unusual." Now, when you gave a statement to the Prosecution -- I'm sorry, to the Republika Srpska MUP, in August 2003, you were asked questions about buses passing by Konjevic Polje. And I'll read some of the question and answer that you gave. "Q. While you were at the check-point in Konjevic Polje, were buses and trucks with persons of Muslim nationality arriving from the direction of Bratunac? And where did they go from there? "A. In reply to your question, I can state that trucks and buses did arrive from the direction of Bratunac, they were loaded with people, but I cannot say what their nationality was because I didn't know. They went on towards Zvornik, Vlasenica, and they returned empty from that direction. "Q. Do you know the number of these trucks and buses that passed through Konjevic Polje? "A. I cannot answer because I did not count them. "Q. Do you know how -- who owned the trucks and buses? "A. The buses and trucks belonged to various companies, but to be honest, I did not read their names." Now, at paragraph 16 of your statement, you also said that you were told that Muslims from Potocari were being transported and that "we should not stop the vehicles in order not to create traffic jams." So my question for you is this: You did not read the names on the buses, you did not count the buses, you could not say whether people on the buses were Muslims, they were Serbs, they were refugees or not -- sorry, strike the last sentence. You did not talk about refugees. Muslims or Serbs. And in fact were you ordered not to stop the buses because you didn't -- you were shouldn't -- you weren't supposed to control or to create a traffic jam. So my question to you is your testimony that you really look at all the drivers and you're absolutely positive that there was no single woman driving a bus?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: This is an intersection that has three directions, Milici, Zvornik, Bratunac. I and my colleague in police uniform were standing at the intersection regulating the traffic in order to prevent traffic jams, and they probably knew where they were loading the passengers and where they were taking them. We had nothing to do with that. As for the statement that I didn't know what nationality the passengers were, of course it makes sense because I never stopped them and never inquired about their ethnicities, therefore I didn't [as interpreted] know if they were Muslims. And I can guarantee you that if you're standing on the road and all the buses are coming your way, you just cannot avoid noticing who the driver is and I never noticed a female driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 10, the witness said, "I didn't check or investigate their ethnicity but I did know that they were Muslims." It was erroneously recorded as witness saying, "I didn't know that they were Muslims."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you confirm that, Mr. Peric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Because in your statement to the RS MUP, you actually said that you did not know whether they were Muslim, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a play of words maybe at the time. I didn't know, I didn't ask, so I didn't know. I could assume that they were Muslims. They were being taken to Bratunac and --

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So I'm a bit confused now. Did you know or you did not know whether people on those buses were Muslim?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I knew that. It was a play of words. I didn't ask them, Are you Muslims or not? But I knew that they were Muslims in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 30 of your statement, you also said this: "Witness KDZ065 testified that upon his arrival at the warehouse, he was beaten by uniformed Serbs and forced to undress with other prisoners. He claims that there were 16 prisoners there in total and that they were beaten by the uniformed Serbs including Nenad Deronjic. That part is untrue. I never brought him to the warehouse." And at 31, you continue and you said: "After being beaten, the prisoners" -- you said that it's untrue what KDZ065 said which is after being beaten, the prisoners were told to put on their clothes. Now I asked you as a first or second question whether you ever went to the warehouse in these days, and you said no. So my question to you now is: What is your basis for saying that KDZ065 is lying when he's talking about events that took place in the warehouse where you said you did not go? How do you know?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I didn't state that I saw these people, let alone that I approached them, that I saw these people being taken away or undressed. I'm stating that no such thing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And my question is exactly this: How do you know that these things did not happen in the warehouse where you said you never went?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I am stating that I did not see that, depending again what warehouse we are talking about. I have no idea what your question is about. You're asking me about a warehouse. What warehouse?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Mr. Peric, this is probably the way the statement is formulated. You --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But at the end of each paragraph, he states the reason why he believes some part of that evidence is untrue. So if you want to ask the question, you need to read out the whole paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I thought I did, but paragraph 30 the end is: "I never brought him in a warehouse."

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you said you never brought KDZ065 in the warehouse, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Except for Resid Sinanovic, I never took in anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yes. And you also said that you never went to the warehouse, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Right. Except for that once when I took Resid over.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness repeat the last thing he said about the warehouse.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat what you said just now, Mr. Peric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you take into consideration -- or if you consider that house where I took Resid Sinanovic to be a warehouse, then that would be it. But aside from that case, I had never brought in anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: All right. I probably should clarify because in the translation we got a little bit lost. At paragraph 30, you are talking about events --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's -- do you have your witness statement with you, Mr. Peric? Can you see paragraph 30 in front of you? Yes. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 30, and now we are talking about, I believe this is your statement, you're talking about the warehouse at intersection of the roads. Now, KDZ065 said that in the warehouse, they were beaten up and forced to undress. He also testified that 16 prisoners were in the warehouse and they were beaten up, including Nenad Deronjic. Now, you said in your statement that this allegation is false. And my question to you is: How do you know, since you've never been into the warehouse? You weren't there. You could not see what was happening in there, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: We are talking about Konjevic Polje here. Is that what your witness was talking about, about Konjevic Polje or some other warehouse?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that -- the distinguished Mr. Costi did not abide by the guidance given by His Honour the Judge to read the entire paragraph 30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, I asked the witness to read out this paragraph 30. Did you read your paragraph -- statement, in particular paragraph 30? And you do not realise what warehouse we are talking about in your statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know what warehouse that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: But you signed this statement?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I wasn't aware of a warehouse being there, in the vicinity of the check-point where I worked. However, in the immediate vicinity of the check-point, I know that there weren't any warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So all the paragraph of your statement dealing with events that took place in a warehouse close to the check-point, in those paragraph, and I think we are talking about paragraph 30, paragraph 31 in part, the first line is talking about beating the prisoners and it's still talking events occurring in the warehouse, you're saying that you're not sure whether paragraph 30 and 31 are talking about a warehouse in Konjevic Polje or somewhere else because there was no warehouse in Konjevic Polje at all?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did not see that there was a warehouse in Konjevic Polje. As far as I was able to see from the check-point. I wasn't allowed to leave the check-point to explore the area, but in the area that was immediately around the check-point, I did not observe any warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So if KDZ065 talks about events taking place in a warehouse in Konjevic Polje, essentially your testimony is these are all lies because there was no warehouse? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Correct. As far as I was able to observe, I did not see a warehouse being there, and I'm telling you from where I was, and that was the check-point. So it is likely that the person isn't telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I see. Now, at paragraph 32, you also said that: "Witness KDZ065 testify -- testified that prisoners were then driven to the banks of the Jadar River where they were executed by four men including Nenad Deronjic. That part is untrue. I never heard of anyone being executed by the Jadar River on 13 of July, 1995." My question to you is, first, did you ever go to the banks of the Jadar River on 13 of July, Jadar River?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I did not go to the bank of the Jadar River at all. I did not have any need for it and I wasn't able to either. At no point in time during the three days I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So your basis for saying that KDZ [sic] is a liar or is lying on this point is that you never heard of it, not that you were there and you could exclude that prisoners were executed there?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did not hear that someone was executed in the vicinity of the check-point, especially not that I don't know how many of them were killed, as this witness of yours seems to state.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Your Honours, maybe this is a good time for the break. Obviously we didn't make it to finish by now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Give me a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll have a break for 45 minutes and resume at quarter past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Costi.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Sir, I would like to go back very quickly to a discussion we were having a few minutes ago before the break. Now, you said at page 65, line 14: "I did not see that there was a warehouse in Konjevic Polje, as far as I was able to see from the check-point. I wasn't allowed to leave the check-point to explore the area, but in the area that was immediately around the check-point I did not observe any warehouse."

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Can we please have P04308, at page 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you three pictures of what I called a warehouse at the intersection. First of all, this picture, I'm talking about the building that is in the blue circle. Now, if you can go to page 45, this is the same building I was talking about here on the left side from a different perspective. Now, I show you another picture and then I ask you the question, which is P00266. As you will see, the next one is the same aerial picture that you've just seen but with a red circle which is the one marked by the witness who was brought there on the 13 of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And for the record, KDZ065 discussed this picture at P00336, pages 78 to 83.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So, first of all, this is the intersection at Konjevic Polje, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, do you recall that building that is marked and circled with a red pen?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So now, this is the building I referred to and KDZ065 referred to when he's talking about a warehouse. So my question for you is: Did you go to that building during those days?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So you never went to that building in these three days?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: While I was at that check-point, I did not enter that building.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Thanks. Thank you. Now, let's move to another topic. In May 1992, you were part of the Bratunac SJB, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: And in your statement at paragraph 11, you discuss the events that took place in Glogova on the 9 of May and you -- you said: "Several days after this incident, we heard that there had also been an armed clash in Glogova where our TO tried to disarm some Muslim extremists who were refusing to surrender their weapons voluntarily. Allegedly, some people were killed in the fighting. I just know that we from the police did not take part in this operation either." So I have two questions here. My first question is: Do you maintain that the police did not take part to the operation in Glogova on the 9th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I did not participate, and based on the stories of the colleagues who talked about it, nobody from the police took part in it. I wasn't in charge of deciding who was to go or not to go or whether they should go or not. I myself was not involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, let me tell you what one person who actually participate to that operation said. And it's the statement of Milenko Katanic at P04374 at paragraph 35. What he said, he said that: "The police, the public security station, also had their armed forces. They were also deployed and they -- and they all had their assignment." So I'm asking it again, you might not have taken part to this operation but do you agree that the police took part to that operation?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I cannot agree because I wasn't the one to make up the roster or to dispatch people there. According to the stories, the police did not participate in this. It was the Territorial Defence. That's what I heard. And it was the volunteers and the army. That's what I heard. I don't know if the police participated or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, talking about these stories that you heard, you said that allegedly some people got killed during the fighting. Is this all you know about what happened in Glogova?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I myself am the one who knows least about Glogova. I was only able to hear things about it. I didn't know anything about it. I don't even know if it happened. I am really not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, this Chamber heard the testimony of one person from Glogova, Musan Talovic, his statement is P03188, and he testified before the Chamber and he told what happened. He described that he was captured, he was brought to the bank of a river with 21 men and one boy, and that the TOs executed the order to kill them and shot at all these men. He alone survived this execution. Not the others. Now, my question is: Do you agree that the goal of the operation was to expel the Muslim population from the village of Glogova? Right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I cannot assert either way. Either that it was the case or not the case. I was not informed about these events. I don't even know when that happened in Glogova, when it was being mopped up or cleansed. I didn't know and I don't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: All right. Let me now move to Bratunac, then. You said in your statement that in April 1992, fewer and fewer Muslims were there, that most of the Muslim left Bratunac on their own accord an in their own vehicles, but there were also those who left by bus in an organised manner. And just to make clear, is it your testimony that Muslims left Bratunac in April 1992 because they decided to leave? They did it voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Well, it is probable that those were left of their own will. They had their own vehicles and they left in their own vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Then you agree that others left not voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: Well, I can confirm this just as much as I can confirm your statement that there were those who left voluntarily. I told you that I didn't know what their reasons were. I cannot claim that they left voluntarily or that they did not because I wasn't there. Quite a few things have to do with what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Now, let's talk about May, still in Bratunac. You said that: "After the incident in Hranca and Glogova, Muslims started leaving Bratunac in large numbers, so that there was a general chaos in the town until transportation was organised. Our patrols were often sent with the military police to escort these buses and trucks which drove to Kladanj and Tuzla." Do you agree with me that these people had no alternative but leaving and they were forced to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the exact reference? Is it the incident at Hranca and Glogova not Kravica and Glogova. Because in that case, the interpretation wasn't correct. Is that paragraph 12?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: It is paragraph 12. And I meant -- and in paragraph 12 to talk about Hranca and Glogova. I'm not sure whether the interpretation said Kravica but I meant Hranca.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was interpreted to us, yes, yes, there was an error.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: So I'm asking you again, you said the Muslims started leaving Bratunac in large numbers, I take it at the beginning of May, after Hranca and Glogova. There was general chaos and transportation was organised, our patrols were often sent to escort these buses and trucks. Now, my question is: Do you agree that these people had no alternative but leaving? They were forced to leave? Right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I don't know what to answer to that question. I didn't participate in that. I don't know if they were forced or they left of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Let me help you here by telling you what a witness said in this Chamber. As KDZ605, he described that he was captured, brought to Bratunac with his family, he was detained both at the stadium, with thousand of others, and then was also brought to the Vuk Karadzic school. He was mistreated for days, separated from his family, and finally deported to the Muslim-held territories. Now, the testimony of this witness helps you to tell me whether you think it was voluntarily or not, the departure of the Muslims from Bratunac in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you if it was voluntary or not. Some left voluntarily, others went on buses. That's at least what I heard. I don't know how they left. I didn't have any contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: But you were a police in town in those days, right?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: A number of them were. I was in a Serbian village called Rakovac in the direction of Voljevica. That's where I was. I wasn't in Bratunac. I spent more time in these Serb villages such as Rakovac, Pobrdje, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have any re-examination, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, two or three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Peric, can you tell us when the departure of the population of Bratunac started and people of which ethnicity were leaving?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: I can't give you any dates, but when the things started brewing, there were also Serbs who were leaving Bratunac because they were afraid, I suppose, but the Muslims were leaving as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You make reference to this in paragraph 6. Can you tell us whether the Serbs were forced to leave by the authorities?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why did they leave?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: They left of their own accord.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And as for Muslims, in the period before May, when the relations deteriorated, were they forced out by the authorities? Did you establish that the authorities were actively involved in forcing the people out?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat the answer due to overlapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you answer the question? Interpreters were not able to hear you because of the overlapping. Could you repeat your answer, Mr. Peric?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really wasn't acquainted with these cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did anyone ask you to expel anyone from Bratunac? And I mean you as the police.

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is missing in the question was if anyone from the authority asked you as the police to expel people, and I didn't mean only authorities. Did anyone ask that of you?

utterances.speaker: MIRKO PERIC
utterances.text: The police did not expel anyone and nobody asked us to do anything in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Peric. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, then, Mr. Peric. On behalf of the Chamber, I thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. You are now free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the circumstances, we do not have any witnesses until Friday morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless there is anything to raise -- yes, Mr. Costi?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if we could go to private session, I would give you the references that we were discussing this morning during the testimony of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Why in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: That's a good question. And probably I can give you the answer in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: It was T 10918 and transcript 10919 of the hearing on 9 of May in the Mladic case, 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. The hearing is adjourned -- oh, yes, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I am an amateur but I wonder how do I treat the references that pertain to other cases that I was not a party to? I would have preferred to have seen this on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Consult with Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. COSTI
utterances.text: If it might help, the Defence has access to the transcript and they were notified by the Registry on the 14th of June, 2013.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will resume on Friday at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
